items.title: EggStreme Malware: Rebuilt Under Scrutiny
items.summary: TL;DR: After we published our first EggStreme research in September 2025, we kept monitoring this malware family, and the development we have seen since justifies an update. Documenting advanced persistent threat (APT, a state-aligned intrusion team) operations matters because these operators depend on staying unseen: once their tooling is public, defenders can hunt for it and find intrusions before they reach their objective. After we published our research, the operators revised their malware architecture and infrastructure, and the timing suggests our report was a likely trigger.

items.title: Introducing GravityZone Exposure Management: Close Attack Paths Before They're Exploited
items.summary: A sysadmin closes the maintenance window with every Critical and High vulnerability patched. One of the remaining mediums sits on a workstation. The workstation's user has administrative rights on a domain controller and signs into it interactively, so their credential material stays in its memory while the session lasts. On the same subnet, a web service still opens to the internet on a port opened during a migration two years ago. None of these findings is worth escalating on its own. Together they are a route to domain compromise, and automated attack tooling now performs the reconnaissance and chaining between steps faster than any ticket queue moves.
